**Serves GL-012. Depends on FR-252/253/254. The HR agent is the first subject.**

## Problem

A composite is a whole product built from components — an HR agent resold to multiple clients. Cloned templates rebuild the duplication problem at the product layer; member refs at versions + frozen glue make a component bugfix a version bump. Operator decision (2026-08-13): wiring lives in each component, so a SAVED composite is already wired — instantiating it is rebrand + client-specific extensions, never rewiring.

## Approach

A composite declares: components (member refs + version constraints), provides, requires, configures (config schema + defaults), extends (named client seams), version (its OWN) — plus the existing rebrand_checklist. The instance record answers "what is client X running" from the catalog.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Composite schema lands: the six fields above, migrated in a NEW version
- [x] HR agent catalogued as a composite whose members are real catalog entries, including the already-published SDK
- [x] Its `extends` seams name `integrations`, `policies`, `ui` — or the deviation from the observed structure is justified
- [x] A composite carries its OWN version, independent of member versions
- [x] An INSTANCE record exists: composite@version + client + config, so "what is client X running" is answerable from the catalog rather than by SSH
- [x] PROVEN: instantiate the HR agent for a fictional second client — rebrand + config + extensions only, no rewiring, no forked component code
- [x] PROVEN: bump a member component's version and show the instance picks it up without touching glue
- [x] The glue-forks-per-client limitation is documented as an accepted trade, with the composite version named as the mitigation

## Notes

Composites are saved MANUALLY and deliberately (operator, 2026-08-13). Loose vs tight completeness decided per composite.
